# YAML Definition Authoring Schema

The YAML workflow engine treats each list entry as a definition. Documentation metadata is
optional and never changes execution behavior.

## Documented Definition

```yaml
- id: stdlib.files.write-text
  title: Write Text File
  description: |
    Writes rendered UTF-8 content to a target path.
  tags: [files, templates]
  extends: stdlib.base
  inputs:
    target_path:
      type: string
      required: true
      description: Output path.
  variables:
    content: ""
  docs:
    variables:
      content: Text to write.
    run:
      - title: Write rendered content
        description: |
          Creates missing parent directories.
  run:
    - python: |
        print("operation")
```

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Required canonical identifier and generated page path. |
| `title` | Optional human-readable page title; falls back to `id`. |
| `description` | Optional Markdown description, commonly authored with `|`. |
| `tags` | Optional labels used in generated navigation. |
| `extends` | One parent definition inherited before local values. |
| `mixins` | Ordered reusable definitions; later mixins override earlier values. |
| `modules` | Relative YAML files loaded into the registry. |
| `inputs` | Typed parameters: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, or `object`. |
| `variables` | Rendered scope values and templates. |
| `run` / `teardown` | Lifecycle operations. |
| `template` | Optional inline template (`engine`, `output`, `body`) that turns the definition into a renderable component. |
| `docs` | Optional descriptions for local variables and lifecycle operations. |

## Structured Operations

`invoke` calls another definition and may iterate a native collection:

```yaml
- invoke:
    definition: docs.definition.template.definition
    arguments:
      definition: "{{ definition }}"
  for_each:
    items: runtime.catalog.definitions
    as: definition
```

`render` calls a template definition (any definition with a `template:` block) and writes
its rendered output to `target_path` in either `write` or `check` mode:

```yaml
- render:
    definition: docs.definition.template.definition
    arguments:
      definition: "{{ definition }}"
    target_path: "{{ output_dir }}/{{ definition.page_path }}"
    mode: "{{ mode }}"
  for_each:
    items: runtime.catalog.definitions
    as: definition
```

Inside a template body, the `component('definition-id', **kwargs)` Jinja helper renders
another template definition and returns its string output for inline composition.

The `generated_pages` operation reconciles obsolete generated definition pages. The
`artifact` operation delegates text and directory persistence to the artifact driver.

## Resolution Rules

Inputs and variables resolve in order: parent, mixins in declared order, then local values.
A non-empty local `run` or `teardown` replaces inherited lifecycle operations. Generated
definition pages show both declared members and this effective resolved API.
